## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column must be fixed before merge: it is populated from the latest `started` event, so it reports a start time for running processes and NULL for ended ones. The documented meaning of NULL is also false for any process whose latest event follows a `started` event.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to `models/processes.sql`, computed from the most recent event per process, and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — `finished_at` holds the start time of a running process — For process 20 in `sources/process_events.sql:9`, whose latest event is `started`, the model returns `finished_at = '2026-01-01T00:01:00Z'`; for process 30, `started` then `cleared`, it returns NULL. The `case` matches `'started'`, while `models/schema.yml:11` says "Timestamp when the process finished." — Consumers read still-running processes as finished at their start time and get no timestamp for processes that ended. — Fix: Either rename the column and its description to `started_at`, or match the event type that ends a process (the source check constraint allows only `created`, `started`, `cleared`).

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the stated meaning of NULL `finished_at` — Process 30 (`started`, then `cleared`) gets NULL, yet the description says "NULL means the process has never been started." The code is `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` over the latest event only, so NULL means the latest event is not `started`. — Consumers filtering on NULL to find never-started processes also get processes that started and were later cleared.
